source_text: Timebant obsetrices Deum. Quidam rationabilem eruditionem in eis viderunt: mediae sunt, masculos et feminas fovent. Sephora — passer — celsiora docet; Phua — rubens / verecunda — mores componit. Mihi utriusque testamenti figura: Sephora legi spiritali, Phua evangeliis Christi sanguine rubentibus. Domos sibi fecerunt quia timebant Deum — non litterae ordo, sed ecclesiae orationum domus. Timens Deum non facis praeceptum Aegypti; vivificas masculum interiorem.
pass_a_gloss: Feared midwives God. Some rational learning in them saw: middle they-are, males and females they-foster. Sephora — sparrow — higher-things teaches; Phua — red / modest — morals arranges. To-me of-both testament figure: Sephora to-law spiritual, Phua to-gospels with-Christ blood reddening. Houses for-themselves they-made because they-feared God — not of-letter order, but of-church of-prayers houses. Fearing God not you-do command of-Egypt; you-keep-alive male interior.
pass_b_english: [[The midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded >> Bible:Exodus 1:17]]. Some before us saw in them the form of rational learning — a midwife’s craft that fosters both male and female births. Sephora, interpreted “sparrow,” lifts minds on the wings of doctrine; Phua, “red” or “modest,” trains manners and honesty. Better still: the two figure both Testaments — Sephora the [[spiritual law >> Bible:Romans 7:14]], Phua the Gospels flushed with Christ’s blood. That they [[made themselves houses because they feared God >> Bible:Exodus 1:21]] makes little sense as bare letter; it fits when fear of God fills the world with houses of prayer. So fear God, refuse Egypt’s command to love the present age, and keep alive the male within — the [[inner person >> Bible:Ephesians 3:16]] healed by good acts and thoughts. [[The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom >> Bible:Psalm 111:10]].
